html:
Semba is the urban music and dance of Luanda, which took shape in the 1950s and 1960s from older Kimbundu songs and rhythms, guitars and the life of the musseques, the poor districts of the city.

Bands such as N'gola Ritmos sang in Kimbundu about daily life and, in hidden ways, about colonial rule, and semba became tied to the nationalist movement. Singers such as Bonga took it to Portugal and the world.

After independence semba was the sound of national pride. In the 1980s it gave rise to the slower kizomba, now danced worldwide, and in the 1990s the faster kuduro grew in the same streets of Luanda. Some trace the name to the word for the belly-bump of the dance, related to the samba of Brazil, a link across the Atlantic.
sum: Semba is the urban music and dance of Luanda, which took shape in the 1950s and 1960s from older Kimbundu songs and rhythms, guitars and the life of the musseques, the poor districts of the city.
